title: Fewest Brackets to Insert
statement:
`text` contains only the characters `(` and `)`. A text is **balanced** if every `(` has a matching `)` after it and every `)` has a matching `(` before it, each used once, like in a correct arithmetic expression.

You may **insert** brackets anywhere. Return the smallest number of insertions that makes `text` balanced. An empty text is balanced.

examples.explanation: The last `)` has nothing to match: insert one `(` at the start (`(())` or `()()`).

hints.nudge: Walk through the text and remember only one number: how many `(` are still waiting for a `)`.
hints.pattern: A counter instead of a stack: every `(` adds one waiting bracket, every `)` cancels one, and a `)` with nobody waiting needs a new `(` inserted.
hints.pseudocode:
waiting = 0; fixes = 0
for ch in text:
  if ch == '(': waiting += 1
  else if waiting > 0: waiting -= 1
  else: fixes += 1
return fixes + waiting
hints.walkthrough: Every `)` that arrives when no `(` is waiting can never be matched by something that comes before it, so one `(` must be inserted for it: count those as `fixes`. Every `(` that is still waiting at the end needs a `)` inserted after it: count them as `waiting`. The two kinds of problems are independent, so the answer is their sum. A stack of brackets would work, but because all brackets are the same kind, a single counter is enough: O(n) time, O(1) memory. Another way to see it: keep deleting the pairs `()` until none are left; what remains is the number of insertions needed.
